1.explanation:
1. packages/components/src/components/content-switcher/content-switcher.js  – This is the core, framework-agnostic implementation that manages adding/removing the “selected” CSS class on tabs. Adjustments here (or its associated SCSS) will ensure that the un-selected tab gets a sufficiently dark border or background color.

2. packages/react/src/components/ContentSwitcher/ContentSwitcher.js  – This React wrapper applies the same CSS classes and renders the tablist and Switch children. We may need to pass through a new modifier (e.g. a high-contrast border class) or tweak the default classNames here so that the updated styles take effect in React apps.

3. packages/react/src/components/ContentSwitcher/ContentSwitcher-story.js  – The Storybook story/channel for ContentSwitcher. We’ll update it to show the new high-contrast variant (or light-variant with updated border) so designers and QA can visually confirm the change.

4. packages/react/src/components/ContentSwitcher/ContentSwitcher-test.js  – The existing unit tests exercise selection and keyboard behavior. We’ll extend or add tests here that render the component and assert that the un-selected tab’s outline CSS property (or computed style) meets the 3:1 contrast threshold, ensuring the fix is test-guarded going forward.
1.bug_scenario:
The screenshots show that, under the default Carbon styling, un-selected tabs in the ContentSwitcher (e.g. “Read” or “Unread”) live on a light-grey background (#f4f4f4) with a very pale border (#e0e0e0). The contrast ratio of that border/background combination is only 1.1:1, far below the 3:1 minimum required by WCAG 1.4.11 for non-text UI components. As a result, particularly in two-tab configurations, users can’t visually group the tabs as a single component—one tab simply looks like text on a page rather than part of a control.

To fix this, we need to increase the contrast on the un-selected tabs’ outline (or background) so that it meets or exceeds 3:1. That requires changes both in the base (vanilla) component and in the React wrapper, plus updates to our stories/tests to verify the new appearance.
